scope: Issue #78 M4.4 crash recovery and provider reconciliation guide revision v2

omitted_axes.reason: Issue #78 exposes application, PostgreSQL, provider and HTTP seams and introduces no graphical UI.

revision_basis.unchanged_axes: All lifecycle, concurrency, public-result, audit, regression, migration and static-registry oracles from v1 remain unchanged.

test_cases.requirement: Authorized provider-first terminal reconciliation has an explicit current path-Workspace/resource authorization -> trusted snapshot routing -> provider observation order and behaves deterministically under current-owner, current-foreign and expired leases.
test_cases.risk: Provider observation can occur before current observation authorization, a terminal outcome can be lost or persisted under a stale lease, or two owners can finalize it.
test_cases.seam: WriteProposalWorkflow.handle(ReconcileExecution), path Workspace binding, WorkspaceResourceAuthorizer, ObservationReferenceResolver, ToolActionStore and independent SQLite provider
prerequisites: AdmissionOutstanding success plus target_not_found, validation_rejected and policy_rejected provider rows
PostgreSQL executing rows with no durable observation
current-owner, current-foreign and strictly expired lease fixtures
counting path-Workspace/resource observation-authorizer, trusted-snapshot resolver, provider-observation and create_ticket sentinels
separate unauthenticated, path-Workspace mismatch and resource-observation-denied variants
steps: For every authorized reconciliation, capture the exact ordered sequence: authenticate and bind the current path Workspace, authorize current Workspace/resource observation, resolve and validate the trusted AuthorizedExecutionBindingSnapshot routing handle, then invoke provider observation with the stored logical execution identity.
Run every observation-authorization failure variant and attempt reconciliation while capturing resolver and provider-observation counters.
Reconcile each terminal provider outcome under each lease fixture; for expired leases race at least two expected-generation recovery owners and a delayed stale owner.
Reload PostgreSQL and SQLite independently and compare terminal and audit state.
expected_results: Every successful path proves current path-Workspace/resource observation authorization succeeds before trusted snapshot routing and before the first provider observation; provider observation is the first external call and uses the stored logical execution identity.

Every authentication, path-Workspace or resource-observation authorization failure returns its typed denial before trusted routing/provider access and has exactly zero provider-observation, create_ticket, dispatch and provider-effect calls.
Current owner records and finalizes; current foreign lease returns ExecutionInProgress without persistence.
Expired lease receives no observation/finalization write; exactly one takeover increments generation once and records/finalizes the exact immutable outcome under the new lease.
Losers and stale owners are fenced, create_ticket/retry count is zero, no second provider lookup is required and public terminal mapping is exact.
evidence_to_capture: per-denial ordered trace plus zero resolver/provider-observation/write/effect counters
terminal HTTP/application projections and independent restart snapshots

test_cases.requirement: NoAdmission provider-not-found recovery creates the first admission only after stale takeover and fresh current write authorization independent of observation-routing authority.
test_cases.risk: Not-found can be mistaken for failed, or a valid observation snapshot can be reused as write authority for an early/unauthorized first write.
test_cases.seam: ReconcileExecution application/HTTP seam, PostgreSQL takeover/admission CAS, current write authorizers and counting gateway
prerequisites: executing NoAdmission seed with a valid AuthorizedExecutionBindingSnapshot
independently controlled current m4r1, Workspace/resource, execution and compatibility write authorities
steps: Reconcile before lease expiry and capture not-found plus takeover disposition.
Expire the lease using PostgreSQL time, race recovery contenders and allow a write retry only after every fresh current write check succeeds independently of the observation snapshot.
Inspect admission, envelope identity, provider ledger/effect and loser counters.
expected_results: Not-found remains ProviderOutcomeNotFound HTTP 202 and lifecycle executing; before expiry takeover is ExecutionNotStale.
After strict expiry one contender changes generation/owner/deadline atomically, reruns every current write check, creates exactly one first admission and dispatches once.

The observation snapshot supplies only trusted routing and no field or provenance from it satisfies a write-authority check; the original logical execution ID/fingerprint survive and losers make zero provider calls.
evidence_to_capture: PostgreSQL time and takeover CAS trace
fresh write-authority decision matrix distinct from observation-snapshot fields

test_cases.requirement: AdmissionOutstanding not-found recovery replays only the persisted byte-identical admission and suppresses duplicates.
test_cases.risk: Recovery can mint a second admission/envelope or duplicate a delayed original external effect.
test_cases.seam: ReconcileExecution, persisted dispatch admission and SQLite idempotency ledger
steps: Observe not-found and race stale takeover contenders.
Release the delayed original dispatch while the winner replays the persisted admission.
Restart the provider and compare admission/envelope/outcome/effect identities.
expected_results: Exactly one takeover wins and no admission is created or replaced.
Retry uses the exact persisted envelope/admission, logical ID and fingerprint.
Provider same-ID/same-fingerprint idempotency produces at most one logical external effect; stale owners cannot observe or finalize.
evidence_to_capture: provider idempotency/effect rows before and after restart

test_cases.requirement: Observation/finalization authority remains structurally separate from write-retry authority across expiry, key revocation, authorization denial and material mismatch.
test_cases.risk: A valid AuthorizedExecutionBindingSnapshot or read/reconcile authority can be treated as write authority, while expiry/revocation can incorrectly block finalization of already-started terminal outcomes.
test_cases.seam: path Workspace/resource observation authorizer, ObservationReferenceResolver, m4r1 verifier, write WorkspaceResourceAuthorizer, ExecutionAuthorizer, compatibility checker, admission/dispatch/gateway and HTTP
prerequisites: found success and all three closed failures
proposal/reference expiry and reference-key revocation fixtures
a valid trusted AuthorizedExecutionBindingSnapshot whose observation path remains authorized while current write authority is independently absent, expired, revoked or denied
independent m4r1, write Workspace/resource, ExecutionAuthorizer and compatibility denial controls
missing/mismatched trusted routing state and all capability/binding/policy identity/version/digest mismatch fixtures
counting retry decision, admission, dispatch, create_ticket, target-lookup, provider-ledger and provider-effect sentinels
steps: With observation authorization allowed, reconcile every terminal outcome once after expiry and once after key revocation.
Deny each observation authority variant and prove denial before trusted routing and provider lookup.

For a provider-not-found execution, retain and successfully use the valid observation-routing snapshot, independently fail each current write-authority seam, then attempt every retry/write path including retry decision, admission creation/reuse, dispatch and gateway create_ticket.
Repeat not-found recovery with missing/mismatched trusted routing and each material compatibility mismatch, then reload proposal, approval, execution and audit state.
expected_results: Every expiry/key-revocation terminal case finalizes with exact success/failure mapping, appends audit and makes zero create_ticket/retry calls.
Observation denial happens before trusted routing/provider lookup and has exactly zero provider-observation and write/effect calls.

When the valid snapshot still authorizes observation routing but current write authority independently fails, observation may return not-found but every retry/write seam is denied with exactly zero new/reused admission, dispatch, create_ticket, target lookup, provider-ledger mutation and provider-effect calls.

Only fresh current m4r1 verification, write Workspace/resource authorization, ExecutionAuthorizer approval and exact compatibility may authorize retry; no snapshot field, digest, identity or provenance is accepted as write authority.

Temporary write denial preserves approved provenance; material mismatch becomes stale/non-executable and requires a new proposal/approval; missing/mismatched trusted routing remains sanitized typed non-terminal and never becomes failed.
evidence_to_capture: per-observation-denial authorization/order trace and zero provider-observation/write counters
valid-snapshot/current-write-denial differential matrix covering every retry/write seam
snapshot-field-to-write-authorizer input exclusion proof and admission/dispatch/create_ticket/provider-effect zero counts
proposal/approval before-after projections, compatibility mismatch matrix and sanitized routing-fault results

test_cases.requirement: PostgreSQL time and generation fencing deterministically decide concurrent recovery.
test_cases.risk: Host-clock skew, lock wait or stale observations can produce two takeover winners or stale finalization.
test_cases.seam: PostgreSQL execution-row lock barriers and typed takeover/record/finalize transitions
prerequisites: current, strict-boundary, stale, changed-generation, foreign-owner and terminal rows
separate takeover, observation and finalization lock barriers
steps: Start operations before the lease boundary and block them before the governing row lock.
Cross or preserve the boundary with an independent PostgreSQL session, release the lock and capture fresh post-lock database time.
Race contenders for non-terminal and provider-terminal outcomes and inspect all returned typed dispositions.
expected_results: Fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time alone decides strict staleness.
Results are only ExecutionNotStale, one Applied takeover, ExecutionFenced, ExecutionInProgress or persisted terminal outcome.
Generation increments once; terminal winner alone records/finalizes and no stale or losing write exists.
evidence_to_capture: lock order and lease boundary trace

test_cases.requirement: Every provider observation has an exact safe application/HTTP projection.
test_cases.risk: Unknown/not-found outcomes can fabricate failure, closed failures can leak provider details or public fields can drift.
test_cases.seam: SupportToolGateway observation Adapter, application result and HTTP serializer
prerequisites: unavailable, timeout, malformed, unknown, not-found, success and all closed failure outcomes
independent result matrix not importing production result/serializer code
steps: Inject each provider observation through application and HTTP seams.
Compare status, outcome/lifecycle/reason or rejection code and complete recursive key sets against the independent matrix.
Inject raw routing, provider ID, envelope, key and internal-error fields and reload durable state.
expected_results: Unavailable/timeout/malformed/unknown return ReconciliationIndeterminate HTTP 202; not-found returns distinct ProviderOutcomeNotFound HTTP 202; neither terminalizes or grants retry.
Success returns ReconciledSucceeded HTTP 200; each closed failure returns ReconciledFailed HTTP 502 with TOOL_PROVIDER_FAILURE and exact allowlisted rejection code.
Every non-terminal and terminal projection has only allowlisted fields and forbidden fields fail closed.
evidence_to_capture: per-row application/HTTP decoded bodies and key sets

test_cases.requirement: Both crash windows recover across independent Knora and provider restarts without duplicate effect, and no-receipt retry uses fresh write authority rather than the observation snapshot.
test_cases.risk: Provider commit acknowledgement loss or pre-receipt crash can strand executing state, duplicate the external action or let observation provenance authorize retry.
test_cases.seam: deterministic crash barriers, PostgreSQL ToolActionStore, observation/write authority seams and independent SQLite provider
steps: Trigger each crash window and capture PostgreSQL/SQLite state before restart.
Restart Knora and SQLite independently, expire the original lease and repeatedly reconcile.

For no-receipt, first keep observation routing valid while denying current write authority and prove every retry/write seam remains unused; then separately grant all fresh current write checks and retry with the same logical identity.
expected_results: Committed provider outcome follows the authorized observation order, one stale takeover, exact-result record/finalize and zero retry/duplicate.
No-receipt remains non-terminal while write authority is denied despite a valid observation snapshot; every admission/dispatch/create_ticket/provider-effect count is zero.
Only after fresh current write checks pass does safe takeover/retry reuse one logical ID/fingerprint and produce at most one effect; repeated reconciliation converges to the same durable outcome.

test_cases.requirement: Append-only audit reconstructs recovery provenance without secrets and provider truth remains independent.
test_cases.risk: Recovery can become unauditable or leak trusted routing/admission material.
test_cases.seam: PostgreSQL audit projection and independently reopened SQLite provider
prerequisites: completed outcomes from TC-01 through TC-07
steps: Restart both stores independently and reconstruct each recovery timeline from PostgreSQL audit only.
Compare provider outcome separately from SQLite.
Scan public/audit evidence recursively for forbidden values.
expected_results: Audit reconstructs actor/authority decisions, binding snapshot, generations, leases, provider observations, retry decision, fencing and terminal result in order.
SQLite remains independently authoritative for provider outcome/idempotency.
No raw routing, envelope bytes, keys, credentials, authority secrets or internal exceptions appear.

test_cases.requirement: The exact candidate passes focused recovery, full regression, Ruff, Compose and clean migration lifecycle verification.
test_cases.risk: Focused recovery behavior can hide schema or M1-M3 regression failures.
test_cases.seam: governed repository verification in the clean Issue #78 worktree
steps: Run clean Alembic upgrade and current, then the focused M4.4 suite.
Recreate/migrate PostgreSQL and run the full repository suite serially.
Run Ruff, Compose config, downgrade/re-upgrade/current and inspect Git status.
expected_results: Every command exits zero with exact invocation and totals recorded.
M1-M3 plus accepted M4.1-M4.3 regressions remain green.
Alembic returns to head and the worktree is clean.

test_cases.requirement: The exact candidate retains the static typed registry and generic fake/SQLite provider seam with no plugin or vendor scope.
test_cases.risk: A green functional suite can hide dynamic discovery, runtime registration or vendor integration expansion.
test_cases.seam: production composition, focused registry contract and exact source-base-to-candidate scope manifest
steps: Resolve CapabilityRegistry through production composition and compare exact identity/version/digest and ticket_lookup/create_ticket typed descriptors before/after restart.
Probe every production application/HTTP surface for runtime registration, discovery, plugin loading, provider selection and vendor-specific adapters.
Generate a content-addressed changed-path/dependency/architecture manifest from source base to candidate and inspect dependency/config/entry-point changes.
expected_results: Registry remains static, immutable and exactly allowlisted with no registration/discovery/plugin operation.
SupportToolGateway remains provider-generic and production exposes only the fixed generic boundary; fake/SQLite remain the only M4 provider adapters.
Manifest binds both SHAs and proves no plugin marketplace, vendor SDK/configuration or vendor-specific integration was added.
